newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends at five year highs, Brent coy.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends at five year highs, Brent coy.

text.p: IPE Oct gas oil rose $7.50 a tonne to settle at $243.25, confirming its position as market leader during a period of low distillate stocks in the United States, brokers said.
The October contract rose to a five-year high of $244 before easing back, supported during the afternoon session by NYMEX heating oil which set a post Gulf War high of $72.90 a gallon.
"Heating oil has broken a new high and it ratched up gas oil to new levels. They are pushing and pulling each other," a broker said.
IPE gas oil at these levels is at its highest for the prompt contract in five years. The next target is $246 a tonne, dealers said.
"This would require heating oil to get a boost above 73 cents and so far it looks a bit anaemic," the broker said.
Distillates were boosted by Tuesday's API data which showed U.S. weekly distillate stocks fell to 112.3 million barrels, down 18.7 million from a year ago.

IPE Brent crude oil futures failed to keep up with gas oil although it found good support at a low of $23.07 a barrel. November Brent was trading 16 cents up at $23.23 a barrel after failing to break through a high of $23.45 a barrel.
"Crudes have been reticent all day to follow the market and gasoline has been neutral. It is still the gas and heat show," the broker said.
